goal: First parallel discovery wave. Four domain agents run concurrently rather than one device per subagent, to find out whether a domain-scoped brief holds evidence discipline as well as a device-scoped one.
scope: Four domains: laundry, climate, av, tools. 21 records to 49.
findings: A domain-scoped agent brief produces records of the same quality as a device-scoped one, at roughly a quarter of the orchestration overhead. The ORCHESTRATOR's 'never give a subagent more than one device' rule was written to stop an agent spreading a fixed research budget thin across a list; a domain brief with an explicit per-record evidence bar does not have that failure mode.

Agents given a hunting-grounds table find the commercial-equivalent product first and work outward, which is what SCOUT step 1 now instructs. The domains where this worked best (tools, laundry) are the ones with a real commercial product line to anchor on.

system_gaps_found.gap: The radios enum had no value for DECT or for proprietary sub-GHz links, so three records carried radios:['unknown'] for radios that were precisely known from their FCC grants.
system_gaps_found.fix: Added dect, proprietary_subghz and ir; backfilled vtech-dm221, thermoworks-smoke-x2 and davis-vantage-vue-weatherlink.

system_gaps_found.gap: Two records cited the same URL twice as two separate sources, overstating the evidence. One of the two was written by the orchestrator, not by an agent.
system_gaps_found.fix: Merged both into single correctly-scoped citations and added a validator rule rejecting duplicate source URLs.

honest_limitations: Records were reviewed by the orchestrator before commit, not by an independent verifier. The review checked schema, source classes, tier calls against the decision table, and that nothing outside data/devices/ was touched — it did not re-derive every claim from primary sources.

Four domains is not a representative sample of fourteen. Laundry, climate, av and tools all have strong dumb options on the shelf today; the wave says nothing about how the brief performs in a domain where almost everything rejects.
surprises: Nothing in this wave forced a change to the ladder. After Chamberlain forced a redesign in phase 0, four domains of new records fitting the existing table without argument is the first evidence the tier definitions are stable.
